decisions.executionNote: Begin symmetric elbow-up approach, pitching open grippers toward tabletop; estimate object heights from RGB before descending.
Align left above red chocolate and right above pale wooden toy, completing downward pitch while staying in separate workspaces.
Refine tabletop alignment from head rays and descend cautiously with both grippers open toward chocolate and wooden toy.
Tracking suggests contact earlier than estimated; lift and recenter using wrist images, correcting tabletop height estimate rather than pushing lower.
Short careful descent and close on red chocolate and pale wooden toy; retention will be checked by lifting and RGB.
Lift both attempted grasps with closed grippers and begin motion toward their respective outer baskets; inspect retention.
Right toy visually retained; transport to right basket. Left grasp missed, so reopen and realign red chocolate with its long axis for a lower retry.
Replan from continuity stop with smaller right-arm travel; hold toy closed. Left approaches chocolate more precisely, still open.
Toy is above the right basket footprint; release and withdraw. Left lowers and closes on the chocolate after wrist-based alignment.
Lift the red chocolate toward left basket while right approaches the right-side watch, with the wooden toy now visible inside red basket.
Carry retained red chocolate over white basket; lower right gripper around watch and close, without assuming retention yet.
Release red chocolate inside white basket and approach left watch. Lift right watch grasp toward middle basket, checking the next images for retention.
Right watch remained on table; reapproach lower. Center both open grippers around their respective watches, then close at near-table grasp height.
Lift both watches with grippers kept closed, then move inward conservatively while preserving left/right separation.
Both watches are visibly retained; position them over opposite halves of the middle basket while keeping arms on their own sides.
Use smaller inward adjustments and a slight lowering after continuity guard; place each watch clear of the middle basket side walls.
Correct rejected tensor with no motion compensation. Separate arms, retaining right watch while pitching it forward toward basket interior.
Correct indexing on zero-motion rejection. Withdraw left gradually and angle retained right watch forward.
Place right watch farther inside middle basket then release; left stays clear to avoid another inter-gripper collision.
Right watch is visible inside blue basket. Withdraw right toward purple chocolate while left approaches the fallen watch after clearance opens.
Retry fallen watch at tabletop height with left arm; right aligns over purple chocolate for later transfer, keeping workspaces separate.
Lift left watch and pitch slightly forward for basket approach. Recenter purple chocolate in right wrist view and close at grasp depth.
Left watch slipped during pitch; reopen and approach its new visible location without rotation during the next lift. Dwell then lift right chocolate vertically.
Both previous lifts slipped. Retry slightly deeper with stationary closing dwell; left retreats a little from basket lip, right aligns with shifted chocolate.
Lift gently with orientations fixed to verify retention. Bring right chocolate away from baskets toward a neutral tabletop transfer location, without crossing arms.
RGB indicates shallow edge grasps slipped. Revise height estimate and approach lower with open grippers, carefully recentering moved chocolate.
Avoid pressing through contact: back left wrist away from basket lip and pitch for clearance. Center right chocolate between finger pads, then close with dwell.
Close left watch with basket-clearance pitch fixed and test a short lift. Move right chocolate gently toward central staging while inspecting retention.
Compensate left angled-gripper tip offset by moving back and lowering before closing. Carry retained purple chocolate to right edge of shared staging area, without crossing center.
Lift centered left watch slowly with fixed pitch. Right chocolate slipped during transport; reapproach its visible tabletop location for a gentler transfer.
Refine right chocolate grasp and test a small vertical lift. Left shifts toward the watch face rather than squeezing the ring center, retaining basket clearance.
Pinch the visible watch face with small wrist-image corrections. Transport chocolate slowly toward neutral center staging while keeping right EE on its side.
Test a slow vertical lift of the face grasp. Lower retained chocolate onto center staging from the right, with no arm crossing.
Release chocolate at neutral tabletop staging and clear right arm. Left changes to yellow wooden toy while leaving the difficult watch visible for a later approach.
Correct zero-motion rejected tensor. Grasp yellow toy with a stationary closing dwell, then test a small lift while right remains clear.
Correct fore-aft grasp offset: reopen and move left grasp rearward over toy body rather than its edge, while right remains clear.
Grasp the toy around its central body and lift gently toward a separate central staging point; keep right arm stationary and clear.
Toy is visibly retained. Carry it toward a front-center staging point distinct from chocolate; withdraw right arm outward to preserve separation.
Set yellow toy down gently at front-center for right-arm pickup, keeping the left EE on its side and right clear.
Leave toy staged and approach central chocolate with left gripper angled toward it, retaining the left EE on its side. Right waits clear.
Lower and move left gripper rearward to seat the staged chocolate between pads, then close and dwell. Right remains outside the shared staging area.
Refine left chocolate grasp away from wrapper edge by shifting rearward and adjusting fingertip reach; keep EE left of center and right arm clear.
Wrist feedback shows the fore-aft correction was reversed. Recenter chocolate with a forward-left translation and restore the prior pitch before closing.
Flatten left grasp to remove unequal finger heights and align over central staged chocolate; right stays far outward, maintaining arm separation.
Center chocolate laterally between pads using the wrist image, then close with dwell and test a small lift; right stays clear.
Lift centered chocolate slowly into left workspace. Begin right approach to staged toy only as the left arm clears the central area.
Chocolate slipped again; correct remaining tilt and approach its current orientation at near-table height. Right approaches only to a separated waiting position beside the toy.
Close on the now-centered, level chocolate grasp and test a slow low lift into the left workspace. Hold right still to avoid contact.
Chocolate appears retained in an edge pinch; carry gently farther left without changing orientation. Right centers over staged toy after left clearance.
Toy was displaced by the low lateral approach; lift right clear before retreating. Regrasp the slipped chocolate deeper between the pads using its latest wrist location.
Recenter chocolate upward within the wrist view with a small rearward correction, then close with an extended dwell. Right remains raised and clear.
Try a shallow angled grasp of the thin chocolate, backing the wrist while pitching fingers forward and lowering cautiously; right stays clear.
Test the angled chocolate grasp with a slow lift toward left basket; move right outward at safe height to clear the central tabletop.
Use an angled approach about the finger closing axis so both pads stay level, compensating fingertip offset while approaching thin chocolate from the front.
Close the level, angled finger pads on chocolate and dwell; test retention with only a two-centimeter vertical lift.
The chocolate still appears unretained. Reopen and make a small purely vertical approach at the level-pad angle, checking clearance before another closure.
At the lower angled approach height, center chocolate between level pads, close with dwell, and test a short lift before transport.
Chocolate now appears seated between the pads. Lift and translate gently toward the left basket with the grasp orientation fixed; inspect retention next.
Previous angled grasp remained too shallow. Reapproach the visible chocolate slightly lower with open, level pads and unchanged arm configuration; right stays clear.
Contact limits further descent. Lift slightly before refining fore-aft alignment, then return to the observed contact height with pads open rather than pushing lower.
Close on centered chocolate with a longer stationary dwell, then test only a small vertical lift before further transport.
The chocolate is centered and visibly seated after the short lift. Transport with smaller fixed-orientation increments to minimize slipping.
Chocolate retention is stable in RGB; continue toward white basket. At safe height, orient right gripper for a level-pad side approach to the staged toy.
Continue stable chocolate transport toward white basket. Angle right fingers toward the staged toy from the right, keeping wrist on its own side and pads level.
Bring retained chocolate over white basket using its angled fingertip offset. Lower right vertically around the centered toy and close without low lateral sweeping.
Release purple chocolate inside white basket, then approach remaining watch from clear front space. Lift right toy gently while keeping its closing command zero.
Both chocolates are visible in white basket. Center and lower left level-pad grasp around remaining watch; carry the right toy slowly while checking its narrow grasp.
Test watch retention with a slow vertical lift. Toy remains visibly retained by its narrow grasp; continue toward right basket with orientation fixed.
Watch remained on table; compensate angled fingertip offset by approaching farther back before closure. Continue retained toy toward the red basket.
Wrist feedback places watch ahead of pads; correct forward before closing. Move retained toy fully over the red basket interior prior to release.
Release yellow toy over red basket and retreat right slowly. Test the centered watch grasp with a gentle vertical lift and unchanged pad angle.
Both toys are visible in red basket. Carry the retained watch upward and forward over blue basket while right withdraws clear for reset.
Watch caught the basket lip and fell. Back left away and upward before retrying; begin gradual right-arm return toward its origin with gripper open.
Approach the watch at its new unobstructed tabletop position, compensating angled-finger reach. Continue gradual right-arm return toward its starting pose.
Center and close on the remaining watch, then test a small lift. Finish the right arm's precise open-gripper return to its observed starting pose.
Right arm is at origin. Reopen left and target the watch face rather than the ring edge, using small wrist-image corrections before closure.
Watch is now centered between the pads. Dwell closed and lift vertically, keeping clear of basket lip before translating forward.
